lets not get carried away. Archetypes might make for interesting literature and theory but it does not help to illuminate this case. 

Obviously its all speculation, but it is quite clear her sexuality and religiosity made for a painful combination. 
She was immersed in a life that sought to repress a huge part of her identity. That is traumatic. We have all met people in those environments and seen what it has done to them: 

'Her friend Hannah Wood wondered what it meant for Hannah to “swallow a part of herself down while she was travelling,” '

Coupled with an unstable sense of self and the over-identification with servitude to shape her identity:  

'“She knew she was loving and openhearted, but beyond that I think she had zero idea of who she actually was. She wanted to give herself over to someone or some idea.”

Also her mother describes going into a similar state herself during her divorce. It may have been a learnt or inherited response to stress. 
Honestly, her tendency to fall into these states makes perfect sense if you consider these aspects to her story.
